title: AD Activity triage - Massive users account manipulation via AD or LDAP
steps: 7. Alert: massive AD or LDAP user account manipulation detected
8. Pull AD and LDAP logs related to user changes in alert timeframe
9. Identify modified users, actor accounts, source hosts, operations and timestamps
10. [Decision] Is the activity truly massive and unusual for this environment
11. False correlation or expected bulk change. Tune rule or thresholds and close as false positive.
12. Determine scope: number of users, types of changes, impacted OUs or groups
13. Classify changes: create, delete, enable, disable, password reset, group membership, attribute changes
14. [Decision] Check actor identity: admin, service account, automation account, or standard user
15. [Decision] Is there a known change window, script, or approved request
16. Confirm with change records or admin team, document as expected and allowlist pattern if needed
17. Mark as suspicious and proceed to triage
18. [Decision] Check time of activity: business hours or off hours, weekday or weekend
19. Review actor account profile: privileges, roles, recent changes, new admin rights
20. Review source: DC or management server or unknown host, internal or remote
21. Look for risky changes: mass password reset, enable disabled accounts, add to high privilege groups
22. [Decision] Check user impact: critical users, privileged users, service accounts, sensitive groups
23. Correlate with other telemetries like firewall, identity related alerts
24. [Decision] Are there strong indicators of compromise or malicious intent
25. Document reasoning and context. Close as benign true positive or false positive.
26. Escalate to security incident. Notify identity or incident response team.
27. Contain actor account: disable or lock, reset password, revoke sessions and tokens
28. Contain impacted user accounts: revert unauthorized changes, reset passwords if needed
29. Contain infrastructure: restrict access from suspicious hosts, block IPs, enforce MFA or admin controls
30. Collect evidence: AD security logs, LDAP logs, backup of directory state, Sumo queries and timelines
31. Identify root cause: compromised admin account, stolen credentials, misconfigured scripts, insider misuse
32. Eradicate: remove malware, revoke compromised credentials, fix vulnerable scripts or tools
33. Recover AD state: restore from backups or snapshots, verify group memberships and critical attributes
34. Harden environment: implement just in time admin, tiered admin model, stronger audit and alerting, change control
35. End: incident handled, lessons learned documented, detections and processes updated

title: AD Activity triage - Multiple user login in same time via RDP on different Servers
steps: 7. Alert: multiple RDP logins same user to different servers

10. Same user to N or more servers in short time window?
11. Correlation or parsing issue. Tune rule or threshold. Close as false positive.
12. Determine scope: number of servers, number of logins, time range
13. [Decision] Check if account is service, admin, or jump account
14. Known and expected admin or jump activity?
15. Confirm with IT or change tickets, document as expected, allowlist if needed

18. Review user profile: role, department, privilege level, recent changes
19. Review source IP: geo location, ISP, VPN or proxy, internal or external
20. [Decision] Check user history: past logins to these servers and from this IP
21. Correlate with other logs: EDR, AV, firewall, VPN, privilege escalation, new tools
22. Indicators of compromise present? Unknown IP, off hours, new servers, alerts, unusual tools
23. Document reasoning and context. Close as benign true positive or false positive.
24. Escalate to security incident. Notify incident response or on call team.
25. Contain user account: force logoff, disable or lock, reset password, revoke sessions or VPN
26. Contain affected hosts: isolate if needed, block malicious IPs or ranges
27. Collect evidence: Windows logs, RDP logs, EDR data, relevant Sumo queries and timelines
28. Identify root cause: phishing, credential stuffing, password reuse, malware, insider misuse
29. Eradicate: remove malware, patch systems, fix misconfigurations, rotate credentials
30. Recover: re enable account if safe, reconnect hosts after validation
31. Improve controls: tune thresholds, update allowlist for known admin activity, add related detections

title: Triage AWS alerts - Configuration Changes - New API Key Created
steps: 5. Yes change is expected and documented
6. No change is not documented or unexpected
9. Start: AWS alert received for configuration change or access change
10. Identify alert type new API key or permission change and time window
11. Pull relevant CloudTrail events for the time window and resources
12. Collect AWS Config evaluations and configuration history for impacted resources
13. Identify actor user or role source IP user agent and MFA status
14. Identify affected services such as IAM S3 EC2 RDS and KMS
15. Determine if alert is configuration change new API key or permission change
16. For new API key created focus on IAM CreateAccessKey and related events
17. For permission changes focus on IAM policy updates role changes and S3 ACL or bucket policy changes
18. For configuration change focus on EC2 RDS security groups and other critical resources
19. [Decision] Is the change covered by a change request maintenance window or automation run
20. Review actor context role department privilege level recent changes
21. [Decision] Check whether change was made by automation tool CI CD pipeline or break glass account
22. Assess blast radius number of resources and data sensitivity impacted
23. Review previous configuration to understand what exactly changed
24. [Decision] Check for other suspicious events around the same time such as failed logins unusual regions or new roles
25. [Decision] Does the change appear unauthorized risky or inconsistent with normal behavior
26. Document reasoning and align with request or maintenance then close or tune alert
27. Escalate to security or cloud platform team for incident investigation
28. If new API key is suspicious disable or delete the key and rotate credentials
29. If permissions changed roll back to last known good policy or configuration
30. If configuration changed revert to previous safe configuration using IaC or AWS Config history
31. Collect evidence CloudTrail logs AWS Config snapshots IAM policies S3 policies and SIEM data
32. Identify root cause compromised credentials misused access keys misconfigured automation or insider misuse
33. Harden IAM and access controls enforce least privilege enable MFA and restrict access key usage
34. Improve monitoring and alerting refine AWS Config rules CloudTrail alerts and IAM access analyzer
35. Update runbooks and infrastructure as code to prevent recurrence
36. End incident and document lessons learned and required follow up actions

title: Triage VPN Connection to Fortinet by User or Time Period
steps: 6. Start: Need to triage FortiGate VPN activity for a user or time period
7. Define username and or time window for investigation
8. Filter logs: type=event AND subtype=vpn AND time within selected window
9. For SSL VPN: include SSL VPN session and tunnel events with relevant logid values
10. For IPsec VPN: include IPsec negotiation and tunnel status events with relevant logid values
11. Extract fields: date time, user, group, srcip, dstip, eventtype, logid, result, tunnel name
12. Filter events by user if specified, else keep all users in the time window
13. Group events by user, tunnel name, source IP, and eventtype
14. Group by logid and result to see success, failure, and tunnel up or down patterns
15. Identify session sequences per user: login, tunnel up, duration, tunnel down
16. [Decision] Check for abnormal login times, burst of connections, or repeated failures
17. Review unusual or new source IPs, geolocation, and client systems for the user
18. Compare current VPN behavior to historical patterns for this user and or tunnel
19. [Decision] Is the VPN activity consistent with normal behavior and known patterns
20. Document findings and close as normal or expected VPN usage
21. Flag as suspicious, open security incident, and notify the security or network team
22. If suspicious: validate user with IAM or HR, consider temporary VPN or account restrictions
23. If confirmed malicious: disable account, revoke sessions, block source IPs, and review firewall rules
